mindmap.comment: Read the mindmap header and its body. mindmap.md#detection: The first node may stand on the line of the header, after whitespace or right after it if it starts with a shape or a character other than a word character.

patterns.comment: A diagram comment starts at %% where a unit starts in the statement context and runs to the end of its line segment; LF, U+2028, or U+2029 ends it. Node text, shape text, and class text own percent pairs inside them. Padding stops before separator-led common comments, which own their following directive-looking text. Neither percent sign of the mark belongs to a directive. mindmap.md#comments: The **mark** of a diagram comment is `%%`, and its value is the text after it. common.md#comment-lines: Comment lines are recognized independently of the diagram's syntax and of the context the lexer is in. common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary: A directive is trivia and not diagram text.

Read the class marker and the following class name. mindmap.md#the-statement-context: `:::`: a `:::` unit; enters the class context. mindmap.md#the-icon-and-class-contexts: So a class line takes the rest of its line segment: `:::c ::icon(x)` has the class `c ::icon(x)`, and `:::a`, U+2028, `b` is a class and a node text on one line, which is rejected.

:icon(, compared case-insensitively, enters the icon context. ) leaves the context; one or more characters other than ) are icon text. mindmap.md#the-statement-context: `:::`: a `:::` unit; enters the class context. mindmap.md#the-icon-and-class-contexts: So a class line takes the rest of its line segment: `:::c ::icon(x)` has the class `c ::icon(x)`, and `:::a`, U+2028, `b` is a class and a node text on one line, which is rejected.

Runs stop before separator-led common comments, and padding never consumes their separator. common.md#comment-lines: Comment lines are recognized independently of the diagram's syntax and of the context the lexer is in.

patterns.comment: The openers are -), (-, )), ), ((, {{, (, and [, in that order. rule 3: The closers are )), ), ], }}, (-, -), ((, and (, in that order. The closer need not match the opener. Strings start only at a unit start, right after the opener; shape text keeps quotes after its first character and has no HTML rule. mindmap.md#the-statement-context: `:::`: a `:::` unit; enters the class context. mindmap.md#the-shape-context: A `"` is a string only where a unit starts, right after the opener: `a[ "x" ]` has the text `"x"`. mindmap.md#nodes-and-shapes: The node text before a shape keeps its whitespace: `a (x)` has the id `a `.

A quote and backtick start a markdown string, closed by backtick and quote. mindmap.md#the-shape-context: A `"` is a string only where a unit starts, right after the opener: `a[ "x" ]` has the text `"x"`.

A double quote starts a string ending at the next double quote, without escapes. mindmap.md#the-shape-context: A `"` is a string only where a unit starts, right after the opener: `a[ "x" ]` has the text `"x"`.

Shape text takes as many characters other than ), ], (, and } as possible; quotes, percent pairs, {, and [ after its first character are text. mindmap.md#the-shape-context: A `"` is a string only where a unit starts, right after the opener: `a[ "x" ]` has the text `"x"`.

patterns.comment: Read node text before a shape as the element name; bare nodes remain labels. mindmap.md#nodes-and-shapes: The node text before a shape keeps its whitespace: `a (x)` has the id `a `.

Node texts: One or more characters other than (, [, ), {, }, and LF, as many as possible, make node text. Quotes, percent pairs, ::, and keyword-like words after its first character are text. rule 7: Whitespace other than LF lies between units. mindmap.md#units-and-contexts: An entity is one placeholder (see [Entities](../common.md#entities)). mindmap.md#the-statement-context: `:::`: a `:::` unit; enters the class context.
